question: A study group debates colonic fermentation of dietary fiber. Which claim is accurate?
options: Human enzymes digest fiber in the stomach.
Fiber passes through the body with no interaction with microbes.
Short-chain fatty acids are produced in the liver from fat.
Gut bacteria ferment fiber into short-chain fatty acids.
gold_answer: Gut bacteria ferment fiber into short-chain fatty acids.
notes: Team-authored original item on colonic fermentation of dietary fiber. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Fiber passes through the body with no interaction with microbes.

claims.text: Colonic bacteria ferment fiber into short-chain fatty acids.

evidence.text: Colonic microbes metabolize fiber into acetate, propionate, and butyrate as fermentation end products.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes bacterial production of the three acids, which entails the claim.

claims.text: All gut bacteria perform identical fermentation.

evidence.text: Different bacterial groups ferment different fibers into different acid mixtures.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes group-specific fermentation, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Fiber supplements cure all digestive diseases.

evidence.text: Symptom scores were tracked in fiber-supplement users with one condition.

claims.verdict_rationale: One condition cannot support cures for all diseases, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Gut bacteria ferment fiber into short-chain fatty acids.

claims.text: Colon cells use butyrate as a preferred energy source.

evidence.text: Colonocytes oxidize butyrate from the lumen as their favored fuel.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage identifies butyrate as the favored fuel, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Fiber is absorbed into the blood in the small intestine.

evidence.text: Fiber resists small-intestinal digestion and absorption, arriving in the colon for bacterial fermentation.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states fiber reaches the colon unabsorbed, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Everyone's microbiota responds identically to fiber.

evidence.text: Microbiota composition was profiled before and after fiber in the volunteers.

claims.verdict_rationale: Profiling responses cannot show all responses are identical, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Human enzymes digest fiber in the stomach.

claims.text: Human enzymes cannot break down most dietary fiber.

evidence.text: Human genomes encode almost no enzymes for fiber polysaccharides, so fiber reaches the colon largely intact.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage states fiber arrives in the colon intact, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Sterile colons produce the same fatty acids from fiber.

evidence.text: Germ-free animals produce almost none of these acids from fiber, showing bacteria are required.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage makes bacteria required, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Probiotics permanently replace the native microbiota.

evidence.text: Probiotic strains were detectable in stool only during supplementation.

claims.verdict_rationale: Detection only during supplementation argues against permanent replacement, but the passage does not settle it, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
